nodes.label: ClusterSingletonManager
nodes.rationale: The per-node actor carrying the election logic; every node runs one but only the host's manager has an active singleton child. It is not spawned by hand — cluster.singleton.start does it at the well-known path proxies address.

nodes.label: singletonManagerPath
nodes.rationale: The proxy finds the current leader's manager purely by path convention (/system/cluster/singleton/manager-<typeName>), so naming it wrong is a silent break.

nodes.label: Host selection: first address-ordered up member
nodes.rationale: Without a role the host is the leader; with one it is the first up member carrying that role — not 'the leader if it happens to carry it', which would leave the singleton unhosted whenever the elected leader lacks the role. Both forms read the same address-ordered member list, so every node picks the same one and the proxy resolves the host exactly as the managers do.

nodes.label: Host-changing event set
nodes.rationale: LeaderChanged, SelfUp, MemberUp, MemberDown/Left/Removed — because the host moves on every transition into or out of up, not only on a leader change. MemberJoined and MemberWeaklyUp are deliberately absent since neither state appears in upMembers(). Before v0.17.0 the trigger was LeaderChanged alone, so a role-carrying member joining below a roleless leader moved the role host without changing any leader: the joiner spawned via its own SelfUp, the incumbent was never told to stop, and the cluster settled on two live singletons.

nodes.label: Unreachability is deliberately not a trigger
nodes.rationale: Every event in the trigger set names a membership fact the whole cluster converges on, so each node computes the same host. Unreachability is not that — it is one node's failure detector saying 'I cannot reach this member', and the member in question cannot hear the peers forming that opinion. A manager reconciling on it would promote itself while the incumbent, told nothing, keeps its child, and no leader moves so nothing resolves it: two live singletons for the duration. The price of omitting it — messages dead-lettering until downing or recovery — is recoverable and bounded; a second live singleton is neither. The lease path is the way to have both, because it is arbitrated by a third party both sides can reach.

nodes.label: restartOnTermination
nodes.rationale: Default true, with a one-second backoff: on the crash-loop death the supervisor's restart budget is already spent, and respawning immediately would reset that budget too, turning a crash-looping singleton into a hot loop. Before v0.17.0 the manager ignored such a Terminated entirely — forwarding to a dead ref with nothing reviving it until a leader change that may never come, and with a lease it kept renewing over a dead child so no other node could take over. Switching it off is an interlock on that node (the manager cannot tell an end state from 'never started'), and the lease is still released so another node may host.

nodes.label: Lease-gated singleton spawn
nodes.rationale: Adds an asynchronous gate over the synchronous reconcile. State transitions run on internal events rather than inline awaits, so concurrent cluster events cannot interleave with an in-flight acquire. On lease loss the singleton stops immediately and the manager retries at once and again on the next host-changing event.

nodes.label: Messages while nobody hosts
nodes.rationale: A proxy resolves the host from its own node's view and the far-side manager decides from its view; they agree once membership does. A message reaching a non-hosting manager goes to system.deadLetters with a once-latched warning naming the singleton, so it shows up in metrics/DevTools instead of being silently dropped. Before v0.17.0 the manager logged per message and discarded — invisible to everything but the log.

nodes.label: acquireRetryIntervalMs
nodes.rationale: Must be positive: there is no off switch, the 5s default applies only to an unset value, and 0 would simply retry immediately — so a non-positive value is rejected up front with an OptionsError.
